_note: Props for the Islamic scholarship styles. In a scene write <prop name="NAME" class="your-class" style="position:absolute;left:..;top:..;width:..px" text="..."></prop>; the bot replaces it with the SVG (params like text, t1..t5 fill the {{...}} slots). Colours follow the palette variables. Animate the listed parts with GSAP using your class: e.g. tl.from(".sc .my-map .city-medina", ...).

arabia-map.description: Schematic map of the Arabian Peninsula and neighbours (Red Sea, Gulf, Hijaz region) with cities: mecca, medina, taif, badr, khaybar, hudaybiyyah, tabuk, jerusalem, damascus, kufa, basra, baghdad, sanaa. Coordinates are real (equirectangular). To zoom on a city, scale/translate the prop; to show a route, draw your own path between city positions (see cityPositions).

star-rosette.description: An 8-point star rosette (two rotated squares in a star) with a core circle and an optional short text (number/term). For medallions, section markers, bullets.

girih-band.description: A horizontal band of 8-point star (girih) tiles between two gold rules. Stretch it (preserveAspectRatio is meet: set width; height follows 10:1). Give each instance a unique id param.

girih-pattern.description: Full-canvas girih (8-point star) pattern for backgrounds. Use at 15-40 % opacity. Unique id param per instance.

wax-seal.description: A red wax seal with a cream ring, a faint star and a short text (e.g. "1 AH", "622"). Stamp it in: scale 1.4 -> 1 with a quick settle.

stamp.description: A red circular rubber stamp, default text HELD. Stamp in: scale 1.6 -> 1, rotate -20 -> -12 deg, opacity 0 -> 1 in 0.25 s.

document.description: A portrait judgment document: cream paper, gold double border, faint ruled lines in the lower half (put your HTML text above it, positioned over the prop). Give it a soft shadow with CSS filter: drop-shadow.

document-wide.description: A landscape judgment document (14:9) for 16:9 videos: cream paper, gold double border, a few faint ruled lines near the bottom. Place HTML text over it.

scroll.description: A horizontal parchment scroll between two wooden rods. Unroll it by animating .scroll-paper scaleX from the centre and moving the rods apart.

book-shelf.description: Five leather book spines on a shelf with vertical titles t1..t5 (short: "Ibn Hisham", "al-Tabari"...). Slide books up one by one as each source is named.

scales.description: Scales of justice. Tilt .scales-beam (transformOrigin 200px 90px) a few degrees and counter-rotate the pans to show weighing; level it for the ruling.

reed-pen.description: A reed pen (qalam) resting in an inkwell. Lift the pen (.reed-pen) and draw an ink line elsewhere to "write".

arch.description: A pointed arch frame (fill + gold outline). Draw the outline with stroke-dashoffset (length about 1900). Put text or another prop inside; rise the camera through it as a transition.

dome-skyline.description: A silhouette skyline of generic domes and minarets (not a specific mosque) on a base line. Use as a horizon, at low opacity, or with a sunrise gradient behind.

lattice.description: A mashrabiya lattice window with star-shaped openings. Animate a light gradient behind it, or its light patch on a wall.

banner.description: A standard banner on a pole for a community or tribe, with a short text (max ~8 letters, e.g. "AWS"). Recolour with CSS: .prop-banner .banner-cloth { fill: … }. Raise it (scaleY from the bottom of the pole).

palm.description: A date palm. Sway .palm-fronds a few degrees (transformOrigin 150px 90px).

city-wall.description: A crenellated city wall with an arched gate (cities, defence, protection). Build it up course by course or slide it up.

timeline.description: A horizontal timeline ruler (ticks every 50 units, long ticks every 200). Put your own AH/CE labels as HTML above/below; slide .tl-marker (translate x) to the date.

lantern.description: A hanging lantern; gently brighten .lantern-glow (opacity) for atmosphere (calm, never flickering fast).

corner-ornament.description: A gold manuscript corner ornament (two rules and a star). Use four, flipped with CSS transforms (scaleX(-1) / scaleY(-1)), to frame a page.
